solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Animal is a sort without tail given extra protection

indicators.note: being protected means being wrapped round, so the word for extra encloses the rest
a thing without its tail has lost its final part, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a sort or kind is a type

explanation.surface: A creature has been bred into a type with no tail and extra armour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given extra protection' reads as armour in the surface, but it tells you the word for extra wraps round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The platypus is the duck-billed egg-laying mammal of Australia, an example of an animal.

clue.text: The old man, holy saint, is supporter of Rome

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father
pi is slang for pious or holy

explanation.surface: A father, a pious saint, backs the Roman church.
explanation.definitionFit: A papist is a (usually hostile) term for a Roman Catholic, an adherent of the Pope in Rome.

clue.text: A subject for discussion making one hypersensitive

parts.note: a topic is a subject to discuss

explanation.surface: A debating subject turns out to be a touchy one.
explanation.definitionFit: Atopic describes atopy, an inherited tendency to allergic reactions, so an atopic person is medically hypersensitive.

clue.text: System of exercises mostly hard for an old character

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: yoga is a system of exercises and postures
H is the pencil-lead abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A tough exercise regime is mostly suited to an old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old character' looks like an elderly person, but it means a letter of an old alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogh is a letter of the Middle English alphabet, a written character no longer in use.

clue.text: Eminence of member of family with superior power

indicators.note: in a down clue, superior means placed above, so this letter comes first

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
a relation is a relative, one of the family

explanation.surface: A family member's prominence comes with greater power.
explanation.definitionFit: Prelation is an old word for preferment or raising to a higher rank, hence eminence.

clue.text: House that's turned over in crime story

indicators.note: something turned over is upended, so in a down clue the letters read the other way
in says the letters sit inside the following words, running across them

parts.note: the letters span the end of crime and the start of story

explanation.surface: In a detective story, a house has been ransacked.
explanation.walkthrough: A semi is short for a semi-detached house, a common British house type sharing one wall with its neighbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-detached house is called a semi in everyday British speech, so it is a kind of house.

clue.text: A rodent rolling over in bracken

indicators.note: rolling over turns something round, so the letters run backwards

explanation.surface: A rat rolls about in the ferns.
explanation.definitionFit: Tara is a name for an edible bracken fern of New Zealand and Australia.

clue.text: Positive declaration once liked except for beginning and end

indicators.note: everything except the start and finish is kept, so the outer letters are removed

explanation.surface: A firm statement was once popular apart from its opening and close.
explanation.walkthrough: FAVOURED loses its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Avoure is an archaic (Spenserian) form of avowal, a positive declaration or acknowledgement.

clue.text: Like a terrible letter presented by a church fellow in ceremony

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are put in the following word, which wraps round them

explanation.surface: A dreadful letter is read out by a churchman during a service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' is not something written but one who lets property: Peter Rachman was a notorious London slum landlord of the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: Rachmanite describes behaviour like that of Rachman, the exploitative landlord, hence a terrible landlord.

clue.text: Naked chaps looking silly somehow sped off to get a coat

indicators.note: things looking silly are in a muddle, and somehow adds a disorder
off signals that the following letters are taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: Unclothed men, looking foolish, rushed off to grab a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: Take S, P, E and D out of NAKED CHAPS, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An achkan is a knee-length buttoned coat worn by men in India, so it is a kind of coat.

clue.text: Ranters upset about nothing turned up

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Angry ranters are bothered about nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Antrorse is a botanical term for hairs or parts pointing forward or upward, i.e. turned up.

clue.text: Fellow with an attempt to restrict a Scot getting hold of land once

definitions.text: Scot getting hold of land once

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man trying to restrain a Scotsman who has got his hands on old property.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole of 'Scot getting hold of land once' is the definition, describing a term from old Scots law; 'an' and 'a' each supply one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In old Scots law a donatary was the recipient of a grant of land from the Crown, a Scot who acquires land.

clue.text: Ache in gym — jump into bath, as before?

indicators.note: one word is placed in the other, which surrounds it

parts.note: PE is physical education, school gym
to ache for is to long for

explanation.surface: Stiff after the gym, someone wants to leap into the bath as usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks an obsolete word: the answer is Spenser's spelling of plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: Plonge is an archaic form of plunge, to dive or jump into water.

clue.text: Fired-up troublemaker having period inside, one of a young group?

indicators.note: having something inside means holding it, so the outer pieces enclose it

parts.note: a term is a period of time
Ate is the Greek goddess of mischief and ruin

explanation.surface: An angry troublemaker has done time inside; is he one of a youth gang?
explanation.walkthrough: The troublemaker is Ate, the Greek goddess of mischief. The 'young group' is a litter of animals born together, not a gang.
explanation.definitionFit: A littermate is an animal born in the same litter as another, one of a group of young.

clue.text: Pet making beastly noise in school

indicators.note: the noise is placed in the word for school, which surrounds it

parts.note: a moo is the noise a cow makes

explanation.surface: A class pet is lowing loudly in the classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun for an animal kept at school, but it is the verb meaning to kiss and cuddle.
explanation.definitionFit: To pet is to kiss and caress, which is what smoothing couples do when they smooch.

clue.text: Concerning vision, artist is held to be prophetic

indicators.note: being held means being gripped inside, so this piece goes within the other

parts.note: ocular means relating to the eyes or sight
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist's work about visions is thought to foretell the future.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracular means like an oracle, uttering predictions, so it is a synonym for prophetic.

clue.text: Something that aids medicinal supply

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a bendy way, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A stock of medicine is a helpful thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like a noun but is read as an adverb from supple, flexibly.
explanation.definitionFit: An adminicle is an aid or support, especially corroborating evidence, so it is something that helps.

clue.text: Small stone to irritate young animal

parts.note: st is the short form of stone, a British unit of weight

explanation.surface: A pebble is thrown to annoy a young creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' asks for the abbreviation of stone; a stone is 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirk is a yearling bullock or heifer, a young farm animal.

clue.text: Unrighteousness gets rash Adam tormented, blessedness finally gone

indicators.note: something tormented is twisted about, so these letters are rearranged
gone means removed, so the chosen letter is taken out of the fodder
finally points to the very end of the word just before it

parts.note: finally picks out the last letter

explanation.surface: Sin brings torment to reckless Adam, whose bliss is lost at last.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the last letter of blessedness, an S, from RASH ADAM before rearranging.
explanation.definitionFit: Adharma in Hindu and Buddhist thought is the opposite of dharma, i.e. wickedness or unrighteousness.

clue.text: Inclination to make a lot pay?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slope or tilt
second meaning: to sell off by auction, a lot being an item for sale

explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' sounds like a large amount, but it is an auction lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A cant is a slope or tilt; as a dialect verb, to cant is to sell goods by auction.

clue.text: Written in haste, a nasty line

indicators.note: the letters are written inside the following words, spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of haste, the word a and the start of nasty

explanation.surface: A cruel sentence was scribbled in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To stean (or steen) is to line a well or similar with stone or brick.

clue.text: Son here is unaccompanied?

parts.note: ecco is Italian for here is

explanation.surface: A boy is here, all alone.
explanation.walkthrough: The Italian theme of the answer explains 'here is': ecco is the Italian for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Secco recitative in opera is sung with only sparse chords, essentially unaccompanied, hence the question mark.

clue.text: More than one snipe gets away, heading off

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its start, and off removes it

parts.note: to get away is to escape

explanation.surface: Several game birds escape, flying off.
explanation.definitionFit: A scape is an old dialect name for the snipe (from its cry), so scapes are several snipe.

clue.text: What sounds like cookin' apple

indicators.note: this says the answer is said the same as the following word

parts.note: coddling is gentle cooking, here with its g dropped

explanation.surface: A cooking apple, written as people say it.
explanation.walkthrough: Cookin' stands for coddlin', to coddle being to cook gently in water; codlin is spelt with one d.
explanation.definitionFit: A codlin is a kind of elongated cooking apple.

clue.text: A kit brought out for treatment of fabric

indicators.note: brought out suggests unpacked and spread about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A set of equipment is taken out to treat some cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikat is a technique of tie-dyeing the threads before weaving, a process applied to fabric.

clue.text: Lathi's wielded in part of India

indicators.note: something wielded is swung about, so its letters are moved around

explanation.surface: Police sticks are swung in a region of India.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick carried by Indian police.
explanation.definitionFit: A tahsil is an administrative subdivision of a district in India.

clue.text: Look briefly, finally climbing on to flat piece of rock

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on to another comes above it
finally points to the very end of the next word

parts.note: a ledge is a flat shelf of rock

explanation.surface: A climber glances up at the end of the climb onto a rock shelf.
explanation.definitionFit: Gledge is a Scots dialect verb for glance or squint, to take a quick look.

clue.text: Prisoner catching disease in the bottom once

indicators.note: catching means trapping, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: roup is a respiratory disease of poultry

explanation.surface: An inmate picks up an infection in his backside, as happened in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Croupon is an obsolete word for the rump or hindquarters, i.e. the bottom.

clue.text: Piece of lead finally fixed to bar

indicators.note: finally picks out the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A lead weight is fastened at the end to a rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' seems to read with lead, but it applies to fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A drail is a weighted fish-hook, a piece of lead used in trolling.

clue.text: Old purse fashioned in calf is cracking

indicators.note: the answer is made inside the next words, sitting across their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run from the end of calf through is to the start of cracking

explanation.surface: An antique leather purse made of calfskin is splitting.
explanation.definitionFit: A fisc was a state treasury or, in Roman times, the emperor's privy purse.

clue.text: Dope getting left in valley

indicators.note: getting here means receiving something inside, so one piece takes in the other

parts.note: gen is slang for information, as is dope

explanation.surface: Drugs are left behind in a valley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' suggests drugs, but here it means inside information.
explanation.definitionFit: A glen is a narrow valley, especially in Scotland.

clue.text: Friends outside tiptop dance-hall

indicators.note: outside means surrounding, so this word wraps round the next

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 written as I

explanation.surface: Mates gather outside a first-rate ballroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A palais (de danse) is a large public dance hall.

clue.text: Exclusive class does badly for fool

indicators.note: done badly means done in a muddle, so the letters are jumbled
for means in place of, so one set of letters stands where another was

explanation.surface: A posh class performs poorly, playing the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: In CLASS, the ASS is swapped out and the jumbled DOES takes its place.
explanation.definitionFit: A closed club or society is exclusive, open only to a restricted set of people.

clue.text: Season not quiet with drink in area of market

indicators.note: with here means having within it, so the season holds the drink
not means without, so the following letter is dropped

parts.note: p is piano, the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet spell with a pint at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: SPRING loses its P to give SRING, which then takes in ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A salering is a ring or enclosure where animals are sold at a market.

clue.text: Faculty curtailed, from that time long ago

indicators.note: curtailed literally means cut short at the tail, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a sense such as sight is a faculty

explanation.surface: Abilities have been cut back since the old days.
explanation.definitionFit: Sens is an obsolete form of since, meaning from that time onward.

clue.text: Material I once got in Devon? Length of it at home brought back

parts.note: che was the old Devon and Somerset dialect form of I

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so these letters are read from the end

parts.note: an ell is an old measure of length

explanation.surface: Someone recalls buying a length of fabric in Devon and bringing it home.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England, where 'che' once served as the word for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Chenille is a soft tufted yarn or the fabric woven from it, a kind of material.
